classification.difficultyReason: Construct an equilateral triangle using equal-radius compass arcs and the equal-side property.

content.prompt: Use a ruler and compasses to construct an equilateral triangle of side length $5\text{ cm}$.

answer.short: An equilateral triangle with all three sides $5\text{ cm}$, retaining the construction arcs.
answer.worked:
Draw $AB=5\text{ cm}$. Set the compasses to $5\text{ cm}$. Draw intersecting arcs above $AB$, one centred at $A$ and one centred at $B$. Label their intersection $C$. Join $AC$ and $BC$, retaining the arcs.

$AB=AC=BC=5\text{ cm}$ because both arcs have radius $5\text{ cm}$. Hence $\triangle ABC$ is equilateral.

spec.description: Authored completed construction with two retained equal-radius compass arcs. The source question supplies no figure.
spec.mathematics: AB=AC=BC=5 cm. C is an intersection of circles centred at A and B with radius AB.
